query: For the paper "Automatic Argumentative-Zoning Using Word2vec" (arXiv: 1703.10152), answer this question: How are the sentence embeddings generated?

drafts: The paper explores three models for obtaining sentence vectors: averaging the vectors of the words in one sentence, paragraph vectors, and specific word vectors [3]. In the first model (AVGWVEC), the word embedding matrix is learned by the classical word2vec algorithm and the vectors in the word sequence are averaged [3]. The second model (PARAVEC) trains paragraph vectors using the distributed memory model of paragraph vectors (PV-DM), an extension of word2vec in which h is constructed from W and D, where W is the word vector matrix and D holds the paragraph vectors, mapping each paragraph to a unique vector [11]. The third model trains specific argumentation word embeddings (BSWE) for a certain category (BAS), and after obtaining the word vectors via BSWE, the same averaging scheme as in AVGWVEC is used [8].

requirements.reason: 答案完整覆盖了论文中三种生成句子向量的方式（词向量平均、段落向量、特定词向量），并分别说明了各模型的具体做法，均与原文对应。[3]支持三模型列表及AVGWVEC细节，[11]支持PARAVEC/PV-DM描述，[8]支持BSWE及沿用平均方案。题目问的是句子嵌入如何生成，答案未超出范围。

cited_sources.text: Three models were explored to obtain the sentence vectors: averaging the vectors of the words in one sentence, paragraph vectors and speciﬁc word vectors. The ﬁrst model, averaging word vectors (AV GWV EC), is to average the vectors in word sequence w =< w1, x2, ...wn >. The main process in this model is to learn the word embedding matrix Ww: P W xi Vavgwvec(w) = 1 w (4) n where Ww is the word embedding for word xi, which is learned by the classical word2vec algorithm [17].

study, BAS speciﬁc word embeddings were trained (BSWE) inspired by Tang et al. [22]’s model: Sentiment-Speciﬁc Word Embedding (uniﬁed model: SSWEu). After obtaining the word vectors via BSWE, the same scheme was used to average the vectors in one sentence as in the model AV GWV EC. 3.2 Classiﬁcation and evaluation The learned word embeddings are input into a classiﬁer as features under a supervised machine learning framework.

The second model, PARAV EC, is aiming at training paragraph vec- tors. It is also called distributed memory model of paragraph vectors (PV-DM) [27], which is an extension of word2vec. In comparison with the word2vec framework, the only change in PV-DM is in the equation (3), where h is constructed from W and D, where matrix W is the word vector and D holds the paragraph vectors in such a way that every para- graph is mapped to a unique vector represented by a column in matrix D.
